titre_exercice: Section D, Topic 3 (au choix) — Essay: A mad cow ran into your school
enonce_intro_markdown: **Section D: Essay Writing (10 marks)**. This exercice corrects **Topic 3**: "A mad cow ran into your school during one morning assembly. Describe what happened next." — a narrative essay, 250-300 words.

questions.enonce_markdown: A mad cow ran into your school during one morning assembly. Describe what happened next. (Write an essay of between 250-300 words.)

rappels_de_methode.texte: A narrative essay in English is organised chronologically, typically in the past tense, with a clear beginning (setting the scene), a middle (the main events, often building tension towards a climax), and an end (resolution); vivid sensory details and varied sentence structures make the narration more engaging than a flat list of events.

questions.corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode
A narrative essay is organised chronologically in the past tense, with a clear beginning (setting the scene), a middle (rising action towards a climax) and an end (resolution), enriched with vivid sensory details.

### Corrigé détaillé

**Model essay (approx. 275 words):**

It was a bright Monday morning, and the whole school had gathered in the yard for the weekly assembly. The principal was in the middle of his usual speech about discipline and punctuality when, suddenly, we heard a loud, terrifying bellow coming from the main gate.

Before anyone could react, a huge brown cow came charging into the compound, its eyes wild and its head lowered as if ready to attack anything in its path. Panic broke out immediately. Students screamed and scattered in every direction, some diving under benches, others climbing onto window ledges, while teachers shouted instructions that nobody seemed to hear over the chaos.

The cow galloped straight towards the flagpole, knocking over several chairs and sending dust flying everywhere. Little Achille, a small boy from Form One, froze in terror right in the animal's path. My heart nearly stopped as I watched the cow charge towards him. Fortunately, our sports teacher, Mr. Ateba, who happened to be standing nearby, bravely rushed forward, grabbed Achille by the arm, and pulled him out of harm's way just in time.

The cow, now confused by all the noise and movement, ran around the compound twice before finally being cornered near the school garden by three men from the neighbourhood who had heard the commotion and come running with ropes. After a tense struggle, they managed to tie the animal securely and lead it away.

Once the danger had passed, an eerie silence fell over the yard, quickly followed by nervous laughter and excited chatter as everyone recounted their version of events. The principal, visibly shaken but relieved that no one was seriously hurt, dismissed the assembly early. It was certainly a morning none of us would ever forget.

*(approx. 275 words)*

### Piège à éviter
Do not simply list the events flatly ('the cow came in, then it ran, then men caught it'): a narrative essay is evaluated on its ability to create tension and vivid imagery, using descriptive details, varied sentence lengths, and expressions of the characters' emotions and reactions.

### Conseil
Always build towards a small climax (here, the near-accident with Achille) before the resolution: this narrative technique keeps the reader engaged and demonstrates a stronger command of storytelling than a purely chronological, event-by-event account.
